blocks.text: 在当今的 AI 格局中，英伟达的影响力怎么形容都不为过。这家公司的芯片是美国发展先进 AI 技术的基石，多年来需求一直超过供给。近年来，英伟达还广泛投资了一批有潜力的 AI 初创公司，在前沿 AI 实验室、新型云服务商、基础设施公司等领域投入了约 990 亿美元的股权。其首席执行官甚至与总统唐纳德·特朗普关系密切。

blocks.text: 黄仁勋如今深陷风波：有消息曝出他与一名疑似中国间谍的女子黄爱丽丝（Alice Huang，与黄仁勋无亲属关系）有婚外情。黄爱丽丝是新加坡云服务商 Megaspeed 的高管，而 Megaspeed 是英伟达的大客户。外界纷纷质疑，这段婚外情是否影响了黄仁勋据称推动向中国出售先进芯片的努力——甚至可能影响了特朗普总统本人在 AI 出口管制方面的决策。

blocks.text: 但到了某个时候，他们的关系变得私人化。2024年6月，就在Megaspeed成为英伟达客户之前，照片显示两人在当地一场贸易展后与其它AI高管在台北的一家酒吧里；第二年，他们据报道还在台北与其他人共进了一顿商务晚餐。但据《纽约时报》援引美国官员的说法，私下里，两人的关系引起了美国政府的警觉——据报道，他们已经监视这名Megaspeed高管数月、甚至更久，正是通过这种方式发现她与黄仁勋有密切接触。

blocks.text: 台湾晚宴仅过了几个月，据报道黄仁勋于2025年7月在椭圆形办公室与特朗普会面，为放宽英伟达先进半导体的出口限制当面陈情。几天后，公司宣布政府已放行其H20芯片对华销售。据《纽约时报》报道，黄仁勋的论点是，让美国芯片进入中国有助于确立美国技术的主导地位，而不是坐视中国芯片发展壮大。在特朗普第二任期对华出口政策早先受挫之后，黄仁勋于2025年开始与时任白宫AI事务负责人David Sacks交谈，后者成为英伟达观点的关键支持者——即向中国出售美国芯片是有益的，《纽约时报》报道称。

blocks.text: CSET 的多门表示，过去两年间，在特朗普政府治下，美国对人工智能出口管制的监管有所松动，部分原因正是黄仁勋本人的游说。但她强调，有一点很重要：“即便中方完全不搞任何情报活动，推动放宽出口管制限制也符合英伟达的利益，也符合黄仁勋的利益。”任何限制从定义上讲都会压制英伟达的业务扩张，切断有助于它继续增长的潜在销售——而它的市值如今已高达约 4.25 万亿美元，仅次于苹果。

blocks.text: 据《纽约时报》报道，今年春天，一份机密备忘录在特朗普政府官员之间传阅，其撰写工作由国务卿马尔科·卢比奥监督。当时正值总统 5 月访华前夕，备忘录警告称，Megaspeed 的那位高管涉嫌代表中国国家安全部从事监视活动。据称她的目标是了解美国的先进人工智能芯片，并设法推动这些芯片大规模流向中国。在周一的新闻发布会上，被问及是否知道卢比奥审阅过这份备忘录时，特朗普说：“我当然会跟情报部门核实。可能提到过。但显然它对我没产生多大影响。”在发布会早些时候，他说自己在访华前并不知晓这一间谍指控。

blocks.text: It’s difficult to overstate Nvidia’s power in today’s AI landscape. The company’s chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump.

blocks.text: “It’s not entirely surprising that the CEO of arguably one of the most important, if not the most important, AI chip companies is the target of some sort of intelligence-gathering from countries like China,” Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET, said in an interview with The Verge, adding that an alleged spy would potentially be interested in “better understanding what the US government is thinking on export controls,” as well as gathering information on Huang’s conversations with the Trump administration, attempting to influence policy, and gathering information on trade secrets like “who’s buying Nvidia’s chips, who’s getting them first, what’s coming next in terms of AI chips.”

blocks.text: The revelation is particularly concerning because of Huang’s lobbying role. He’d been trying to convince the Trump administration and Congress to loosen export controls for sending advanced semiconductors to China, ostensibly so that Nvidia could sell more chips. We now know this was happening around the same time that Huang was spotted at the Taiwan dinner with Alice Huang in May 2025, according to Culper Research, which shorted Nvidia’s stock earlier this year. That dinner occurred shortly after Nvidia had shared the Trump administration’s new restrictions on its China-specific H20 chips in April.

blocks.text: Just a couple months after the Taiwan dinner, Huang reportedly met with Trump in the Oval Office in July 2025 to plead his case for loosening export restrictions on Nvidia’s advanced semiconductors. Days later, the company announced that the administration had blessed sales of its H20 chips to China. Huang had argued that spreading American chips to China would help establish US technology as the standard, rather than allowing for Chinese chips to grow, according to The New York Times. After setbacks earlier in the second Trump term in export policy to China, Huang began speaking with then-White House AI czar David Sacks in 2025, who became the key advocate for Nvidia’s view that selling American chips to China would be beneficial, the Times reported.

blocks.text: CSET’s Dohmen said that during the past two years, the US has seen a light loosening of AI export control regulations under the Trump administration, driven partly by Huang’s own lobbying. But it’s important to note, she said, that “even without any kind of intelligence operations from the Chinese side, it is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions.” Any restrictions by definition stifle Nvidia’s business expansion and cut off potential sales to help it grow its already stunning market cap — which is currently about $4.25 trillion, second only to Apple.

blocks.text: Huang’s relationship with Trump is also particularly relevant here. The president lavished praise on Huang during a speech last year, saying that until recently, he hadn’t even heard of Nvidia, and then he wanted to break it up. But after meeting Huang, he said, he understood why it would be difficult to re-create the company he’d built. More recently, Huang put Trump on speakerphone when the president called him during an appearance onstage at the All-In Summit, publicly displaying his close access to the Oval Office.

Her reported goal was to learn about advanced AI chips in the US and try to influence them being made available to China on a large scale. Asked if he had known about the memo reviewed by Rubio at a press briefing on Monday, Trump said, “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. blocks.text: On Sunday, Huang wrote an internal memo to Nvidia employees — some of which are his own family members — writing, “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” He then addressed Nvidia’s board, partners, and shareholders, adding that he is “fully committed” to leading the company and “will work to earn back your confidence.” This weekend, Nvidia’s board of directors launched an independent investigation into the national security allegations. Huang will not have control over the participants in the investigation, and Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
